Shatter Me: Series Two #1

Privește-mă

Tahereh Mafi, Shauki Al-Gareeb (Translator)

4.25
84,985 ratings13,667 reviews
Rate this book
Goodreads Choice Award
Nominee for Readers' Favorite Young Adult Fantasy & Sci-Fi (2025)
Plină de acțiune palpitantă și o poveste de dragoste sfâșietoare, de tip slow burn, Privește-mă este primul roman young adult dintr-o nouă serie plasată în universul „Atingerea lui Juliette”, bestseller național și internațional, care cere un răspuns la o întrebare disperată… Cine suntem când nu ne privește nimeni?

În această distopie de tip sci-fi, James Anderson avea un plan. Sau o jumătate de plan. Tot ce contează este că a reușit să facă lucrul pe care fratele său mai mare, faimosul Aaron Warner Anderson, nu l-a făcut niciodată: să se infiltreze pe Insula Ark, ultimul refugiu al Restaurației. Niciun intrus nu a pătruns în fortăreața regimului autoritar, dar James este înăuntru. Desigur, într-o celulă de închisoare, dar, în ceea ce-l privește pe James, o victorie e o victorie.

Au trecut zece ani de la căderea Restaurației, când notoriul duo format din Juliette Ferrars și Aaron Warner Anderson a condus o rebeliune mondială și a stabilit Noua Republică a Vestului. Însă Restaurația este gata să facă o mișcare devastatoare și are asasinul perfect pentru această misiune.

Rosabelle Wolff avea un plan. Ea mereu are un plan. Pe Insula Ark, unde supravegherea constantă este prezentată drept siguranță, chiar și emoțiile trebuie trăite cu precauție. Iar când i se dă un ordin de a ucide, ea nu ezită niciodată.

About the author

Tahereh Mafi

82 books78.2k followers
Tahereh Mafi is the New York Times and USA Today bestselling author of the Shatter Me series. She was born in a small city somewhere in Connecticut and currently resides in Santa Monica, California with her husband, fellow author Ransom Riggs. She can usually be found over-caffeinated and stuck in a book. Shatter Me is her first series, with television rights optioned by ABC Signature Studios; Furthermore, her first middle grade novel, is on shelves now, and Whichwood, its darker companion, will be on shelves November 14, 2017.

4.35!

"Adam wanted peace, Warner wanted justice. But I'd realized at a young age that you can't have peace without securing justice, and when you're living under tyranny you can't secure justice without violence. I didn't want to like a passive life."

Spin-offs usually are a hit or a miss—some love them more than the original series, while others think that their association with the original series is a crime. For me, Watch Me was in the former. NOW HOLD ON! This series will probably never outshine the absolute masterpiece that Unravel Me and Ignite Me were, but if you compare Shatter Me as a first book and Watch Me as a first book, you can clearly see that Watch Me excels.

What Shatter Me suffered from is really absent from this one, and obviously, these are the basic things you would expect from the spin-off because the author's writing style would improve a lot if you're comparing her first work with her latest—and that is what I liked!! Seeing the progress that she made, and that made this book overall so enjoyable. And yes, it had its shortcomings and faults, but I cannot lie when I say how much I loved it. Like, it was everything I wanted it to be while also being very different from what I wanted it to be. One thing is for sure: a lot of you would not like it, and the reasons would be valid. But if you have a strong connection with the past characters, you will definitely have the best time of your life with this one.

“In my dreams I am safe; I have a strong hand to hold; a door to lock against the dark; a trusted ear into which I whisper my fears. In my dreams I am patient and kind; I have room in my heart for more pain than my own. I am not afraid to smile at strangers. I have never witnessed death.”

Tahereh's writing in this one was exactly what I wanted—it was humorous but also well-balanced with a few moments of high stakes, and very fast-paced. Like me and Hoda devoured this book in a day or two. It was very fast-paced, coupled with short chapters, which made me feel like I was making a lot of progress lolll. It was also very addicting—like, I could not stop reading it even if I wanted to.

There were a few things from the previous series that I had a problem with here, like the repetitive nature of some sentences and the vague nature of some of the plot points. But I didn't pay much heed to the latter because, according to Mafi, this is going to be a relatively longer series. So I think as we move forward, the plot would fit right in. But I would say that I had high expectations for it, and it did not disappoint me. Considering how many of the new anticipated releases disappointed me this year, it felt good to read one that did not.

"It’s simple logic: if we believe our choices are our own, if we do not know we are being bent into obeisance, we will not be be tempted to revolt"

The characters were easily the part that really overshadowed everything in this book. I feel like all the characters were done right in this one, and I had no problem with any of the characters—which is why I am rating it so high—because they were the ones who had the most page time. They were the saving grace of the book, and they were definitely the ones who made reading this book such an enjoyable experience for me. I love how, with all these years passed, none of them lost their charm and made me feel the same way that they did when I was reading the original series.

“There's a rage that lives inside me ... The rage of a child still too young to fight the monsters when they came calling.”

Rosabelle, I'm starting with her because she's the only new character that I want to talk about. I would say for a main character, she was very different but also not (?) at the same time. I liked the assassin role and her purpose for being where she was—it kind of gave her character much-needed depth. But I feel like there is still much work to be done. Don't get me wrong—some of the things that followed Rosa's character were very intriguing and have a lot of potential, but I just don't really love her that much. And that is understandable because she's new in a sea of characters who we know, love, and want to read about. I feel like with the following books, she would join them. One thing that annoyed me about her was her constant mention of being dead on the inside—like, it got too much. I did enjoy reading her point of view though. I wanted to read James's more, but hers didn't really put me off.

“You live your life as if nothing can hurt you even though your body is covered in scars”

James Kent, he's 80% Warner, 15% Adam, and 5% himself lmao. I loved him!! He was like a younger version of Warner! A head-over-heels lover, but unlike Warner, he was a bit dumb. I feel like he didn't really see the extent of the whole situation when he made his decisions. However, I really liked his loyalty towards his family and how much he loved and cared for them. I also loveeed his banter with everyone and his humor—it was so fun to read his point of view, and he even made Rosabelle's point of view more enjoyable. I laughed so much reading this book, and it was mostly because of him. He's such a cutie patootie, and I really want to see what happens to him in the next book because umm... the way book 1 ended... I am high-key concerned. Also, is anyone else surprised that he's charming and has a way with his words?? Yeah, that’s what I thought.

“Aaron Warner Anderson is a living legend.”

Aaron Warner, I think I accidentally and unknowingly screamed whenever he appeared in this book. His scenes and the aura that they radiated >>>>. He was so mad in this book—like literally, he was mad the whole book because of James's actions and would only be a cutie in front of Juliette. Like that woman has him wrapped around her finger. But yeah, I loved how he had everything figured out—like that one scene where James is dumbstruck, but Aaron knew what Rosabelle was going to do and said it—chills. I also obviously loved the few scenes we got of him with Kenji—they literally make my day. The ending—ahahaha yeah, I fully support him and whatever he did. Also not Aaron wanting to kill James for making Juliette cry.

“I'm living Kenji's dream right now," I whisper, still petting the bird's head. "Except for all the blood, I'm basically a fairy-tale prince. All I need is a musical number and a fairy godmother.”

Juliette, Kenji, Nazeera and Adam, Juliette was so sweet—like she deserved a hug. The way she cried sm because James was missing was so sweet. She wasn't really in this book a lot, so I don't have a lot of thoughts, but I love her. Kenji, I loveeeeee him so much—my man was desperate, so heartbroken and so damn funny. That whole scene of him and Winston moping had me creasing. When he said he couldn't be compared to Arabs I LOST IT. But yeah, it's no surprise that I loved him and I loved his banter with James. Nazeera, I wish she was in this book more, and I want her to be in the next books because I miss her the most and Tahereh you better fix the shit you pulled. Adam—guys idk I think his wife really made this man likeable because why was I smiling at them and feeling smthign for them? They were cute.

“When there's something you want but can't have, you can be patient or creative. Choose a path.”

The romance, it was good because, I mean, we are getting an MMC who's a mixture of Kenji and Warner. I liked the chemistry that they have and the things that James said were swoon-worthy. I love how both him and Warner fell so deep in love with women who tried to kill them lmaoo. I feel like while Rosa was in love, she still was able to keep her emotions in check and try to do what she intended, but James was more obsessed and that would jeopardize their missions. But the chemistry and tension was there, and the slow burn was there too. I just didn't feel the spark that I was expecting. Maybe it'll be prominent in the next books, but I was expecting a bit more. It wasn't disappointing though—like, it was enough to keep me invested and enough to make it an enjoyable experience for me.

“Hate that Warner is probably right, that profanity is probably a failure of the mind, that only idiots need to rely on foul language to express themselves properly-or whatever stupid shit he said to Adam that one time.”

The plot, this was the only disappointing part. It didn't really hinder the experience for me—I'll explain. The plot took a back seat in this book. It was missing. And although we had a plotline, it wasn't enough because it wasn't progressing in the way a plot should in a fantasy/dystopian. But it didn't really ruin my experience to that extent, because that gap that it made was mostly filled by the characters. And I imagined this book like a prologue to this series, a way for us to get familiar with the changes to the world and to the characters. I liked the plot points set up and would like to see it be explored as the series progresses. But I feel like I set my expectations in that way when I was reading this book, because the way this book was set—with a light plot and heavy character development—was a very nice way for me to familiarize with the changes made and the things that may happen next.

Overall, a really great start to this spin-off!

'watch me' is actually about Rosabelle and James staring at each other half the time. that’s why it’s called 'watch me' … because of the constant staring at each other …

kenji and aaron literally carried the book—my strong kings, ugh 😌💅🏻🎀

this is gonna be long so buckle up.

this book can be easily divided into two parts. my rating for the first half would be 3.5 stars. that part is funny (thanks to james), with some high stakes, new discoveries on every page, and, of course—escape.

the second half though? a solid 1.5 stars. it’s slow, it’s repetitive, and it drags on with nothing new happening. by that point, we already know what's coming, and it's just like, okay, cool, i guess we’re just waiting for the inevitable? where’s the fun in that?



this isn't a bad book per se, but i also feel like it doesn't have that particular 'shatter me' feel that made reading the original series so much fun. i only felt excitement about what james might do in the first half. other than that, my only interest was in the original characters, or when they were mentioned or their interactions.

which brings me to my point: if the whole point of this book is to cash in on the love for the original characters, then why the heck are we being introduced to a whole new cast? we’re supposed to care about them, love them, feel things for them, right?

but i didn’t (or at least not as much as i hoped to)

⚡︎"Welcome back to Shatter Me universe, where chaos reigns supreme,
Trauma’s the tether, and hope is a dream.
Redemption is violent, yet we’re caught in the blaze,
Fighting through the ashes, igniting the haze"⚡︎‏

"I’ve been here before—different shoes, same ground ,There’s something about this world... it felt like home” And just like that,We’re back in the Shatter Me world, where the stakes have never been higher. Takes place in the new-republic Waffle leading Rosabelle Our new FMC fights for freedom intensifies as she navigates betrayal, survival, and unexpected alliances. When James enters her world, everything shifts. Secrets are uncovered, lives are shattered, and the battle for a future begins. Hold tight, the storm’s only just started.

⁀➴ Let’s Break Down the Cast, Shall We?~

♂ "Introducing James, the golden retriever buddy you never knew you needed – all heart, no filter." (✿◠‿◠) Enters James Anderson (yes, that James—Adam’s little brother), who pulls up like he’s starring in Survivor: Revolution Edition I was here for him. His charm, his resilience, and his overall sense of, like, not being a total jerk? Sigh. He’s the boy we didn’t know we needed, but once we got him, we were hooked. trust me when I say, he's like a ticking time bomb of pure potential. He’s always doing the most, but somehow it always ends in hilarious, yet heartwarming, disaster. Like, he’s the kind of guy who would steal your last cookie, crack a joke, and somehow make you forgive him because he’s just so damn likable. has a thing for gummy bears🧸ིྀHE is all aaron's looks and kenji'personality as I predicted. the infiltrator with a secret agenda, because obviously no one else is after the truth about Ark Island. He clashes with Rosabelle, but somehow they connect. His “resilience” and “kindness” are the shining lights in a world of darkness. So original, right? Honestly, James is basically Kenji’s clone, but with more emotional depth and darker twists. Every chapter that was from James' POV had me like "Keep talking, buddy."I sure he sures a lot lol!

♀ Rosabelle Wolf- Part-time assassin, full-time identity crisis 🥷⚔️ Emotionally repressed, morally gray, violently maternal. Kills people by breakfast, cries once a year. Knife before life, runs on guilt and unresolved trauma,Trained to Kill, Forgot to Feel. If Juliette was the sad poetry girl, Rosabelle is her angry nihilistic cousin who has trust issues and a sharp object collection. The “I’m dead inside” girl. Trained killer meets tired elder sister trope. She’s got the emotional walls of a 14th-century castle and enough unresolved trauma to power a Netflix limited series. the tragically complex heroine with a mysterious past. She spends the whole book grappling with her inner violence and oh, the redemption arc we’ve all been waiting for. And of course, her relationship with James makes her question everything—her beliefs, loyalties, you name it. It’s all about that “power of choice” and “courage to change,” because who doesn’t love a good self-discovery journey? Honestly? Ugh. Honestly. I couldn’t click with her. I get it, her life is tough, and she’s had a hard go of it. But there’s just not enough spark to her character. She has so much potential, but it’s like she’s holding all her emotions in a box, and I’m just left waiting for her to open it.Anyway sigh- Maybe things will unravel in book 2 hopefully.

⟢Kenji (HE 👏 IS 👏 SO 👏 BACK.)
Ahhhh, Kenji. The legend. The king. You want comic relief? You got it. You want someone who’s genuinely loyal, hilarious, and just a blast to be around? Yeah, that’s Kenji. Kenji is the guy who always brings the vibes, and without him, this entire story would just be one big emotional breakdown. He’s got that charming side that’s impossible to resist, and honestly, if I could steal him from the book and put him in real life? I would. He’s like that friend who can roast you to the core but also throw in a “but I love you” right after. Iconic But here’s the best part: Kenji raised James—I mean, it’s clear. They have this insane, charming energy that makes you smile every single time they interact. Like, their banter? Top-tier. They’re both quick-witted, sarcastic, and have a sick sense of humor. I love their dynamic because it’s like they’re cut from the same cloth!!
-KENJI X NAZEERA ENDGAME OR WE RIOT.
The chemistry?? The banter?? The tension that was absolutely there in Defy Me and Restore Me???I SAW IT. YOU SAW IT. WE ALL SAW IT. 👀🔥 🕯️ dearest Tahereh Mafi 🕯️
please…
from the bottom of my broken, book-loving, Kenji-adoring heart—
give my SHAYLA a happy ending.
🧷 More side chracters -Clara Wolff,Lieutenant Soledad,Sebastian Rivers,Adam Kent,Elias,Jing,Winston,kip, castle...

✪-The Pulse of the Narrative Rosabelle and her sister Clara struggle to survive on Ark Island, a harsh and controlled place. Rosabelle, hardened by loss, is forced to confront the violence within herself to protect her sister. When she crosses paths with James, an infiltrator from The New Republic, their fateful encounter sparks an uneasy alliance. As they uncover dark secrets about The Reestablishment’s plans, they must navigate betrayal, trust, and their own demons. In The New Republic, Rosabelle faces her past and struggles with the possibility of redemption. With stakes rising, she must make a final sacrifice that will shape her future and the fate of the world.
🪶 Plot Devices
Klaus, the Phantom Mastermind, controls everything from the shadows, manipulating minds with chilling precision. In the New Republic, his influence is everywhere, leaving Rosabelle and James caught in a web of control and paranoia. Meanwhile, the surveillance, Nexus, and Vial shape their journey toward escape and redemption, each representing a force of manipulation, hope, and the struggle to rebuild in a fractured world.

🖇️Kenji & James: Partners in Chaos 𐙚
Sarcastic charm meets reckless energy in a duo made for disaster.
Trouble finds them, but laughter and loyalty keep them close.

🖇️ The Banter-
Every jab is laced with care, every insult a hidden hug.
They fight, tease, and bond in the most chaotic, heartfelt way.
“One last thing, James.”
“What?”
“Don’t touch her. Unless it’s to kill her.”
“Excuse me?”
Kenji: “Oh shit, twist! this is better than the movie night interesting🍿

╰┈➤ Things That Left Me Hanging-
~A lot felt incomplete, especially when it came to Adam and his relationship dynamics. It left me wanting more backstory and closure.listen, we’ve got to mention Adam once just to get it out of the way. I am happy how far he had come, wanted to see more of him—his journey with Alia and his family also lacking of james and adam's bonding. So many unanswered questions!
~Some pacing issues. Like, are we running or are we dragging our feet in trauma mud?
~The Chemistry: It’s developing, but right now it’s very much “will they, won’t they” and I'm just like can we get to the good part already? it’s playing the slow burn card, and I’m not mad... but I’m impatient.
~Repetitive inner monologue (we get it, she’s sad and full of knives).

✏ Final Verdict!?Felt like déjà vu wrapped in chaos. I missed this world—its broken glass beauty, its heavy hearts and quiet wars. James? A wildfire I didn’t know I needed. Rosabelle carried knives and numbness, but never quite reached me. The plot had moments, but not enough soul. It was all noise, no melody. Still, something about the ache felt familiar. 3 stars—for the nostalgia, for Kenji’s warmth, and for the hope that book two might finally crack Rosabelle’s shell open.
🩷 For: Shatter Me stans,complex girlies , Warner simps, and Kenji truthers!
💥 Rating: 3.5 knives-to-the-heart out of 5 -Brainrot in 4K. Dolby Digital. Maybe even IMAX.

With a heart heavier than a leaden tome, I must confess: 'Watch Me' didn't just disappoint; it plunged me into a literary abyss. A single star feels like an act of charity, a mere whisper of the frustration this book induced. I lost count of the moments I teetered on the brink of a DNF, a desperate escape from the suffocating boredom. Even a younger, more forgiving version of myself would have recoiled. The writing, oh, the writing! It possesses an immaturity that left me not just unimpressed, but actively yearning to launch the book across the room. And let's not even begin to dissect the relentless, repetitive sentences, as if the English language were a barren wasteland devoid of nuance. This book felt less like a story and more like a cruel exercise in linguistic monotony. Avoid this book at all costs.
And the plot? A phantom, a wisp of a thing, barely discernible beneath a deluge of overwrought quotes, clearly designed to elicit hormonal flutters from an audience I can only assume is comprised of emotionally stunted teenagers. Instead of crafting a coherent narrative, Mafi seems content to hopscotch between vaguely dramatic scenes, prioritizing fleeting moments of manufactured 'intensity' over genuine character development. James, the supposed 'sunshine boy,' and Rosebelle, the obligatory 'dark girl,' are nothing more than hollow archetypes, devoid of substance or depth. Ironically, the few glimpses we get of Aaron and Juliette, mere supporting players in this theatrical disaster, cast the protagonists into stark relief, exposing them for the pathetic shadows they truly are.

"𝗦𝘂𝗿𝘃𝗲𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆..... 𝗢𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗰𝘆. 𝗢𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗰𝘆"
ten years after the fall of The Reestablishment, Ark Island remains a bastion of oppressive surveillance. Within this tense, isolated world, a dangerous game unfolds. James Anderson, determined to succeed where his brother failed, infiltrates the regime, aiming to penetrate their formidable defenses. Amidst the constant scrutiny, an unlikely and volatile connection sparks between James and Rosabelle Wolff.

"𝗦𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝘄𝗮𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗼𝘂𝗰𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗳𝗲𝗲𝗹 𝗶𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗿𝗻. 𝗜𝗳 𝘄𝗲 𝘄𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗱, 𝘄𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗵𝗶𝗺 𝘁𝗼 𝗼𝗯𝗲𝘆."
James Anderson, Aaron Warner's baby brother,a man with healing power, a fleeting vision of blue eyes and brown hair, the kind of ephemeral cuteness you glimpse on a bus or in a library, only to vanish into the ether of 'what could have been.' But let's be honest, his charm is quickly overshadowed by a staggering lack of... well, anything resembling intelligence. The man's emotional range is that of a damp sponge, and his cognitive abilities seem to have taken an extended vacation. Case in point: his instant, inexplicable infatuation with Rosebelle, a woman who, in their first encounter, attempted to redecorate his throat with a sharp object. And his initial, utterly baffling assumption that she was an AI? Seriously? He looked at a human being and thought, 'Yep, that's a robot.' It's a level of brain-melting stupidity that defies all logic, leaving one to wonder if he accidentally swapped brain cells with a goldfish. He is so stupid that you cant help but feel annoyed.
Rosebelle Wolff: a serial killer with high-tech skills masquerading as a 'dark, cold-hearted woman,' only to reveal herself as a fragile, wilting flower as the narrative progresses. The initial promise of a ruthless, enigmatic character quickly dissolves into a portrait of weakness, a stark contrast to the image she so desperately tries to project. Orphaned and burdened with the responsibility of protecting her sister, Clara, her engagement to Sebastien, feels less like a romantic entanglement and more like a desperate attempt to secure a lifeline in a world that seems determined to crush her.

“𝘚𝘩𝘦’𝘴 𝘯𝘰 𝘧𝘳𝘢𝘨𝘪𝘭𝘦 𝘪𝘯𝘯𝘰𝘤𝘦𝘯𝘵. 𝘕𝘦𝘪𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘥𝘰𝘦𝘴 𝘴𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘴𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘳 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘰.”

“𝘞𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘮𝘢𝘬𝘦𝘴 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘬 𝘐 𝘩𝘢𝘷𝘦 𝘢𝘯𝘺 𝘭𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳𝘢𝘨𝘦 𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘳 𝘩𝘦𝘳?” “𝘉𝘦𝘤𝘢𝘶𝘴𝘦 𝘴𝘩𝘦’𝘴 𝘣𝘦𝘦𝘯 𝘴𝘢𝘺𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘺𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘯𝘢𝘮𝘦 𝘪𝘯 𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘥𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘮𝘴.”


P.S.Perhaps, in the grand scheme of literary tastes, 'Watch Me' simply isn't for me. I acknowledge that its blend of dystopian intrigue and tumultuous romance will undoubtedly resonate with many readers. Maybe I've simply outgrown the tropes and stylistic choices that seem to captivate a younger audience. Or maybe, just maybe, this book's flaws transcend generational divides. Regardless, while I may stand alone in my vehement dislike, I can't deny that Mafi possesses a talent for crafting worlds that ignite fervent passions. Just, unfortunately, not mine.

2 stars. Yes. You read that right. TWO.
Yeah, I know—I can’t believe I gave it a two either...

MY BIGGEST COMPLAINT??
WHAT DO YOU MEAN KENJI AND NAZEERA BROKE UP.
HUH???
Not only are they NOT married with babies, they’re not even TOGETHER??? I’m legit sobbing. You just… ripped out my heart and laughed while doing it??
WHY.

Like please. Tahereh better be plotting their reunion because Kenji deserves the damn world, and right now he’s just out here cracking jokes to hide his heartbreak, and I'm too soft for this. DO YOU KNOW HOW MUCH I LOVED THEM??? My babies. My beautiful disaster babies.

That said… I was LIVING for the crumbs of Aaron, Juliette, and Kenji. My lil dysfunctional trio. They carried. Aaron simply breathes, and the book becomes tolerable.

And Adam??? Listen. I was a certified Adam hater™ back in the day, but… now???
I GET IT.
He was hurting, traumatized, just trying to protect James. And now he has his own lil family, and I’m just over here like yes king, live your peace era. His bond with his kids?? So sweet. Also—Aaron??? Helping take care of Adam’s kids??? Excuse me while I sob into my pillow.
Character growth is REAL.

BUT. Let’s talk about James.

WHY is James so distant from Adam??? I get it—everyone loves Aaron. But c’mon, Adam literally spent half his life protecting James , and now it’s like he’s been shoved to the side. NO. RESPECT THAT MAN.

Now… Rosabelle. Look, I'm tryna be fair here. She’s a bit like Juliette in the OG books—you’re either vibing with her or you’re slowly losing brain cells. I was this close to skipping her POVs. I swear every chapter was her staring at something like:
"I feel nothing. I am broken. I must save Clara. Repeat."

Girl, get a grip.

James tho??
I actually liked him. He’s funny, chaotic, and kind of dumb in an endearing way. Reminded me of Kenji with a little extra ✨baby energy✨. But let’s be real: he’s not cut out for survival, lmao. Neither is Kenji. If they weren’t protected by plot armor and our love, they’d be dead in three business days.

Also. Can we talk about the fact that James and Rosabelle’s chemistry was giving wet cardboard?
Zero spice. No tension. Nothing.
Just two confused teens staring at each other like:
“Do I trust you?” “Idk, do I trust you?”
I was begging for a plot twist, a kiss, a spark—ANYTHING. But nah. All we got was endless eye contact.

AND THEN KLAUS??
Bro is literally AI gone rogue. Emmaline 2.0 vibes but somehow less interesting??? Just... existing in the background like a ghost in the Wi-Fi. Klaus was supposed to be scary, and I was just like... okayyy sips tea.

BUT ENOUGH OF THAT.
Let’s talk about the real stars.

AARON WARNER.
That man continues to own my soul.
The way he treats Juliette???
UNMATCHED.
The soft kisses. The worry. The MY WIFE lines. I swear my heart exploded.
Every crumb of him being a husband? A soon-to-be dad? Give me more. Inject it into my veins.

“Do I get to meet her?”
“No,” everyone shouts at the same time.
Juliette shrinks back, surprised.
“I’m sorry,” Warner says instantly. He blanches. “Forgive me, love. I didn’t mean to shout at you.”


LIKE. STOP IT. I'M GONNA CRY.

Also:
✧ Aaron cooking pasta for Adam’s kid = 10/10 dad material
✧ Kenji pushing Aaron out of the way 'cause of the unborn baby = I can't
✧ Juliette & Kenji having junk food slumber parties = core memory unlocked
✧ James getting roasted by Kenji and Adam = sibling energy YES

But yeah. To summarize:

First half? Not bad. Fast-paced, some good laughs, new worldbuilding.
Second half? Snoozefest. Dragged. Empty. I was praying for it to end.

And Rosabelle x James? I’m sorry, but no spark = no stars from me.

The heartbreak over Kenji x Nazeera not being endgame genuinely overshadowed everything else. Tahereh better fix this because right now??? I’m in pain.

Final rating: 2 sad little stars.
Because Warnette, Kenji, and Aaron's fragile sanity were the only things holding this book together.

Tahereh... please don’t break what’s already shattered.
We’re tired. Give Kenji his happy ending. Let James learn some survival skills. And please… plot next time, thank you.

3.5 stars

For me, Shatter Me is canon. Watch Me is just fanfiction Tahereh wrote for James Anderson’s fans 🤡 Because what was this? Like, I have no idea where to even begin. Is Tahereh playing with our feelings? Because this was so unserious. The plot is fine, I can see it getting better, but naming an artificial intelligence villain KLAUS? If Klaus Mikaelson were real, he’d be rolling in his coffin and getting his daggers and his siblings’ army ready to burn this thing himself. The name was so weird and out of nowhere. The fascists and the Reestablishment thing is boring so far—it gets interesting here and there, but not enough to keep my attention. And honestly, the parts that I enjoyed the most were of the Shatter Me gang! Those chapters and the OG Shatter Me gang literally breathed life into this book, carried the interesting parts on their shoulders, and I wouldn’t even be giving it 3 stars if there were no scenes or involvement from them.

Rosabelle is even more insane and depressed than Juliette. At least with Juliette, her backstory and trauma were revealed slowly as Shatter Me progressed, but here Tahereh was giving me whiplash with this girl. I feel so bad for her, her sister, and I want her sister to live, because those scenes where they talked about food like it was some out-of-this-world thing, because they were always hungry, kept starved by Klaus and his army, were heartbreaking. She is dead inside, and the only thing that’s keeping her alive is her need to save her sister and James because he’s handsome? We don’t know what her powers are yet, but I have some theories cooking in my brain.

“I’ve been fooling people all my life. You’re the only one paying attention.”


James was just a child in Shatter Me, so I was excited to see how he grew up, who he took after in terms of personality and all. And consider me shocked when I realised he’s the stupid and reckless version of Kenji with no survival instincts. This man was naïve enough to go to an island where all the fascists were building an army led by the most dangerous AI, and had the nerve to think he could take it all down by himself. I can see depth in his character, but so far it’s only about how he feels suffocated because he’s the baby of their family. I understand that, but he was also raised by Aaron Warner—the most meticulous and intelligent person in their world, the legend himself—and he still behaves like this? He’s so unserious and funny.

“The girl is every inch the backstabbing, cold-blooded mercenary everyone told me she was. I should probably get my head checked.”


Rosa and James have forced chemistry so far. It feels like Tahereh locked them inside a room and told them that either they fall in love or die. I was waiting for maybe Warnette vibes, because my standards are in another universe because of those two—but it’s not even close to that. James fell for her way too fast. Even when she looked like an AI doll to him, he was on his knees for her, even though he knows she’s going to kill him. He’s blindly and stupidly in love, and Warner knows this—and it was funny how he and Kenji taunted him for it. Rosa feels something for James, but it’s all a mess right now. She’s in the New Republic, playing staring contests with James. It was something, maybe to add some tension and heat, but it did nothing for me. I don’t know which direction their romance will take in the next books, but I have faith in Mafi.


⚠️ THERE WILL BE POTENTIAL SPOILERS IN THIS REVIEW FROM NOW ON!!


Shatter Me babies!

Oh, the feeling of coming home to these characters years later and seeing them all as grown-up adults. It was the best nostalgic homecoming, the most wholesome feeling ever. I love these characters with all my heart. Tahereh, though, destroyed some parts for me. The Watch Me in this title was for watch me make your favourite characters suffer for another book. But seeing them laugh and joke and live together was the best thing in this book. Kenji making fun of Warner, Warner being Warner, and all of them in one room as this one big happy family who now make dinner plans and everything? It healed me.

Kenji ignores this, adding, “Warner loves me, too,” around a bite of popcorn. “Sometimes it’s a little too much, you know? It’s always Oh my God, Kenji, you’re amazing, you’re my best friend, don’t tell Juliette but I love you the most—”
“How is it that every time you speak,” Warner cuts him off, “you have food in your mouth?”


I can never get enough of their hilarious dynamics 😭😭

Warner being a good big brother to James, raising him and loving him so much that he became an inspiration for James—it was everything.

“Warner rarely let me out of his sight. He tucked me under his wing, teaching me and training me. Rebuilding me. And by virtue of living in his home I’ve seen glimpses of him most people wouldn’t believe possible. Softer versions of him; laughing versions of him. Loving versions of him.”


Warnette, Warnette, Warnette! I just always wanted to see them as adults and I’m so happy to see how they’re doing. Aaron Warner as a daddy? Someone put me on a ventilator because even the thought of it is making me breathless—but it’s happening in reality now. We all know he is daddy material, so kids are necessary, and don’t you dare say you never imagined Warner with a little girl, braiding her hair, playing peekaboo with her, making weird smily faces at her to make her laugh. Warnette is having a baby!!

“I’m sorry,” Warner says instantly. He blanches. “Forgive me, love. I didn’t mean to shout at you.”
She softens, beaming at him like he’s some kind of baby animal. Sometimes I think she sees Warner in a way literally no one else does. She seems to think he has no thorns at all.


Warner as a husband? I am in my room doing witch-level manifestations to make a man like him find me in this real life. He’s so fine as a husband: so attentive, loving, caring, and patient, always looking out for Juliette and the baby. Someone please give him the best domestic husband award 🥺💘

“This man lives to worry about you. It’s his favorite thing to do. Between worrying about you and talking about you and frolicking through fields aggressively shouting your name at wildlife, I’m surprised the man has any time left to fuck with the world.”


Kenji and Nazeera not being a couple in Watch Me is the biggest betrayal by Mafi. She never gave us their exclusive book, but she also snatched their happy life away from their hands. Seeing Kenji still trying to be the jokester of their group even though he’s hurting inside and missing Nazeera? It was not needed. Absolutely unnecessary and destroyed parts of this book for me. He is one of the most precious characters in this series and she chose him to hurt? I want to go back to my Shatter Me world now.

“Oh my God,” he says, appearing and disappearing, his invisibility glitching. “I think I’m dying. Did she get more beautiful? How did she get more beautiful?”


Brendan and Winston? My heart can’t take it, because what do you mean Brendan broke Winston’s heart? I refuse to believe this nonsense. It never happened. Only Adam and Alia are living the almost-perfect white picket fence fantasy in this world, and I’m happy for them—but others also deserve that same happiness.

Ever since I finished Shatter Me, I was living in this delulu perfect world of happiness, where all my favourite couples had the perfect happy life, where they were rebuilding their world, but no Klaus existed. Where Warnette had lots of kids, Kenji and Nazeera were happy, got married and Kenji almost fainted seeing Nazeera walk down the aisle. They have a son, and that son has his eyes on Warnette’s daughter, and Warner is almost on the verge of killing Kenji. Where Winston and Brendan adopted dogs.

Six books of torture and heartbreak weren’t enough, so Mafi invented another series to put them through hell? I still have faith in Mafi, so she’d better do justice to Kenji and Winston in the next books or else I’m going to riot. As a first book in a new series, Watch Me was not so bad. It’s interesting and has potential. But I want more!

🍬 james warner ᝰ.ᐟ james is so funny, i can’t even deny it ✋, his inner thoughts made me laugh out loud multiple times. however, aaron and kenji weren’t wrong when they called him a child, because that’s how he was acting throughout the entire book. his relationship to kenji, aaron, and adam though 🥺 overall, i feel like he’s just a watered-down version of kenji 🤷‍♀️

🤖 rosabelle wolff ᝰ.ᐟ she was so boring 😭 i don’t think she said more than a page of words in the new republic. here are the things that i know about her: 1. she has perfect porcelain white skin (😐) 2. she has the most mesmerising blue eyes ever (istg this was mentioned at least 50 times in the book) 3. her sister is getting tortured by the re-establishment 4. she’s dead inside - the amount of times this was mentioned: “i’m dead inside,” “i’ve been dead inside for 4 years,” and constantly telling her own mind to die 😐 we get it.

🧡 kenji and nazeera ᝰ.ᐟ NOW WHAT HAPPENED TO THE WHOLE REASON I PICKED THIS BOOK UP. why why why!!! they were so perfect together ugh. honestly i think tahereh is going to have them get back together in the next book or next next book in the series (please please please 🙏). but UGH the way kenji talked about nazeera even when they were broken up… and was jealous 🤭🦋

👑 aaron and juliette ᝰ.ᐟ tbh i’m not the biggest fan of them but i’ll always appreciate the way aaron always puts juliette first no matter what, and him protecting her with his life 🥹 juliette was pregnant in this book, girl seriously deserves a BREAK 😭 OH MY GOSH next book we’ll see daddy warner?? 😋😋

overall, this book was definitely extremely addicting to read, and i feel like tahereh could seriously do something with the way the plot is going. especially with all the traitors in the new republic and the new technology that the re-establishment has. i also would love some more chemistry from james and rosabelle as well.

“Aaron Warner Anderson is a living legend.”

hell yes he is 😫

I'm such a hypocrite, I don't deserve to be saying such things after saying bad things about him in the last three Shatter Me books but I SWEAR Shatter Me, Unravel Me, and Ignite Me Warner are PEAK, and I just really need a reread.

but anywhoooo, this book was one of my most anticipated of the year, and of course I was a little nervous after how I hated the ending of the Shatter Me series, but this book had SUCH a different vibe than any of those.

(there might be some 'hints' as to what happen in this book in this review so proceed with caution)

Also, the cover on this thing is gorgeous. I got the exclusive one from Amazon with the iridescent edges and she's STUNNING.

The Plot

Since it's been so long since I read the og series, it took me a while to remember what things were, like the Reestablishment (now that one was embarrassing once I figured it out I felt so dumb), the New Republic, and even some characters. That did end up in me flipping back and forth a lot, but I mean, that was on me, so it didn't really hinder any of my enjoyment towards the book.

The beginning was fast, and I did enjoy that since I was not in the mood for something slow, so we were just shot right into the world. The first half was definitely my more preferred half, just following James and Rosabelle as they got off of the island and all that, but the second half just became more tedious and confusing, which is disappointing, because I thought it was set up nicely to be a good double cross or something like that and it just....fell flat (for reasons that will be said later in this review)

ALSO I don't know if my book had a misprint or something, but the ending felt SO abrupt. I don't even remember how the book ends (that's my fault guys 😄) but I do remember being almost done with the book and there still being so much plot left, so I don't even know.

“It’s simple logic: if we believe our choices are our own—if we do not know we are being bent into obeisance—we will not be tempted to revolt.”

The Characters

here's where I can finally....talk 🫠 and it's very unfortunate

I've actually seen a lot of people saying Rosabelle was annoying or boring, and I for once have my own opinion and think that she wasn't that bad 😭 I enjoyed her chapters and character, and learning more about her backstory. I love ruthless characters that are forged to be that way (not that I like that they were forged to be that way, but they're just interesting to read about I swear 😭) like I genuinely was entertained and interested in reading her inner thoughts as she struggled to remember and maintain her own sense of self and being.

Now James.....I did like him in the beginning, but oh my goodness he was immature. I'm guessing that's got something to do with his trauma (I lowkey remember NOTHING about his backstory) but I swear he was just being stupid at times. He's legally not even a child anymore in this, but he very much acted like one. His jokes were so repetitive and unnecessary at times. I enjoyed it in the beginning and I was like 'oh, so he's like Kenji!' but it became SO MUCH. He's a knock off Kenji. He's a combo of Warner and Kenji, but if you dumbed those two down and he had like no Warner in him except by relation.

and he pissed me off SO BAD during the ending, because WHY was he so trusting to the girl he literally kept calling a serial killer? he was choosing her over his family which makes no freaking SENSE. He was just so naive, and I do feel bad, but buddy's brother is literally Warner and I KNOW Warner raised him better than that. AND WHEN HE TALKED BACK TO WARNER? I wanted to hit him because he knows NOTHINGGG.

DILF WARNER DILF WARNER. I don't know why but I didn't even think about him being older in this book and UGGGHHH I love him so much bro. He's just so smart, amazing, incredible, attractive, and UGH. HE'S LITERALLY THE BLUEPRINT BOOK GUY. AND THE WAY HE CARES FOR JULIETTE IN THIS I CANNOOOOOOT

We didn't really see Juliette as much in this, and I admit, I was a Juliette hater, probably still would be, but she was sweet in this. Look guys, the last three Shatter Me books ruined everything for me, I swear I still liked them all.

Kenji my sweet was also better, his jokes are better than James's anyways, and at least he's actually got some rational thoughts, unlike that guy. Poor Kenji though, I felt so bad 😭

“Growing up with these two has ruined me for regular relationships. I want what they have”

don't we all, James

The Romance

this is where it gets bad

I literally have an update during this book where I was like 'oh, I'm liking the progression of this romance, it's not too fast' blah blah blah, but that was before James and Rosabelle described each other's physical features 15 MILLION TIMES.

I was fine with it at first because I can accept attraction at first sight but I don't need MULTIPLE paragraphs describing James's perfect brown hair, freckles, chiseled body, or her GHOSTLY blond hair and just as GHOSTLY pale skin with her unblinking ORBS. Like please. I was actually getting so annoyed because it continues throughout the entire book. Their hearts were always racing when they saw each other, skin tingling, blah blah blah. And I KNOW Rosabelle was trained better than to lust over a handsome guy, like I can understand her, but she's literally a serial killer 😭

Not only that, but there was hardly any chemistry. When they were together in the beginning, they wanted to kill each other of course, and then when they make it back to the New Republic, James is suddenly more interested in her and wants to spend all his time with her? It made no sense. They do more looking at each other than talking anyways.

And then we get back to the ending again, which continued to make NO. SENSE. as I said, they do more staring than talking, so hooooow did we get to the point where we're going against our family to save a serial killer? It was just so stupid.

“Doll Hands is a serial killer. My pants were getting tight over a serial killer. Kenji is going to love this.”

Like okay, I get the line is trying to be funny, but please

“I know that she's right-handed? She recently discovered she doesn't like tomatoes? Direct sunlight sometimes makes her sneeze?”

he literally knows NOTHING ABOUT HER

then of course Warnette was just their perfect Warnette selves with a little twist hehehe. I'd suspected it, but I didn't actually think it would happen, it's so odd reading about my babies like that.

anyways, it may seem as if I hated this book, but I did rate it 3 stars so I didn't necessarily haaaate it, more like have many criticisms. I don't agree with the overall rating of this book, but to each their own I guess. I'll obviously read the next one because duhhhh

3 stars

“I know you meant that as an insult, so consider yourself lucky I like you enough not to murder you for disrespecting my wife.”

⊹ “I don't want to live in fear of my hands, my head, the collapsed star that is my soul. I don't want to live every day only for the promise of death.”


🎧┆who’s afraid of little old me? + my strange addiction

⤷ my thoughts
overall i did enjoy this! and it was so nice being back in one of my fav universes. i thought this was a fun and quick read! short chapters>>> the plot was entertaining, though the whole nexus thing and how the reestablishment had complete access to peoples’ minds was creepy af. the government’s literally watching your every move 🫢 interested to see how tahereh mafi goes with all that.

⤷ characters
🧸 james
i loved him so much in this book and seeing him all grown up, you can detect the influence from aaron and kenji on him 🫶 i swear he was unintentionally funny and i loved his inner dialogue. i almost lost it when he started monologuing to the raccoon 💀 also why does he lowkey remind me of oak from tfota? probably just bc they’re both the fmc’s younger brother (figure) lol.

🪞rosabelle
yeah so i can see why people were calling her bland now… she wasn’t a terrible character, and i did find her backstory—growing up in the reestablishment and everything—interesting. it’s just that she didn’t show much personality. after a while tho, all her reminders to herself to “be dead inside” and “you’re dead” got a little annoying. but then she meant it literally? it was sad to see how the reestablishment messed her up but girl are you alright🧍🏻‍♀️ ngl tho i feel like she started growing on me a little bit at the end.

🪽james and rosa
erm enemies to lovers, you say? 🙈 from the start james was already infatuated and flustered by her beauty and her strikingly pale complexion and hair, blue eyes, blah blah and vice versa. gah i just hated the insta-attraction. the way they were trying to kill each other one second then feeling each other up the next lmao. but i’m rooting for them nonetheless!

🕊️ og characters
oh. my. gosh. how i missed these characters 🥹 seeing the og trio—juliette, aaron, and kenji—made my heart so happy! and juliette being pregnant omg? i’m so happy for them 🫶 warnette are gonna be parentsss aww.
i forgot how much i loved kenji!! he’s my fav character, tied with aaron i think. but him and nazeera better get back together or i swear…

⤷ concluding thoughts
i had a great time being back in this universe and you know i’ll eat up any spinoffs of this series even tho they’re not necessarily necessary 🤭 i’m excited to see where tahereh takes this plot!

thank you to my fav girl jasmine for reading this with me! yapping about it with you made it an even better experience 🫶 i think it’s safe to say that this buddy read made up for our other one that ended up disappointing haha! i love you endlessly 🥹

➳ kenji—walmart's version ☆

well... i am happy to be back in this world with tahereh's writing. i find her books easy, fun, and fast-paced. being in the worst slump is not helping, as i am unable to fully enjoy anything. however, this was refreshing.

⌞rosabelle “i don't remember her last name”⌝


she reminds me so much of juliette. i found her character to be a typical mary sue, self-insert. a lot of this book is her worrying about her sister and talking about the re-establishment. the insane number of scenes with her talking about “not eating” and “starving” went nowhere. i feel like there was potential, but nothing was explored. (i know this is book 1, so i hope she has better development in the later books).

⌞james “motherfucker” anderson⌝


take a damn shot every time this hoe says “motherfucker”. surprisingly, i think james had it worse than rosabelle in terms of archetype, development, and deportment. i understand what mafi was trying to portray, especially with the insane popularity from the OG series. however, i felt like i could not connect to anyone here, especially since a lot of these characters feel like the temu version of the OG's. unlike kenji, james' character was chaotic, messy, and his dry humor did not hit for me. (again, this is just book 1, so i am sure things will get better).

⌞OG characters⌝


i love them. no one will ever make me not love them. (this includes adam). i don't wanna hear it.

now... ms. mafi will pay for what she did to my babies kenji and naz. give them their own book, now!!!

"it’s simple logic: if we believe our choices are our own—if we do not know we are being bent into obeisance—we will not be tempted to revolt." ᡣ𐭩.ᐟ
⭑𓂃 ⌗ my thoughts

being back in the shatter me world was quite comforting — especially since it was really fun to read about the og trio (particularly Kenji!! idgaf ab Warner) again and I genuinely think it was the best part of the entire book. i'm never forgiving Tahereh for what she did to Kenji & Nazeera though. as for 'watch me' itself, I think it was a pretty easy read to get through especially since Tahereh's writing style is quite addictive. but while I enjoyed james's pov, I found rosa's one to be painfully boring. also I felt like the world wasn't fully developed, and there are still many unanswered questions...like, world building who?!

⭑𓂃 ⌗ characters

ᝰ.ᐟ Rosabelle Wolff

she kinda reminded me of Juliette, but other than that, I feel like we don't know anything about her except the fact that she's been dead inside for YEARS, because she brought it up like every five seconds. but NO, girl, YOU'RE NOT. it doesn't even hold up — Rosa was basically infatuated with James the very first time she laid her eyes on him, and got flustered every single time he looked at her, and as far as I'm concerned neither of those things is being numb nor emotionally shut off. moreover, she basically melted when he so much as breathed and what was this 'he makes me feel alive' speech?! girl, you've known him for like 2 days 😃 her chapters were also longer & there were more of them so was that a misery! she was so completely and utterly bland like girl GET SOME PERSONALITY!!

ᝰ.ᐟ James Anderson

James, babe, if you say that you'll destroy Rosa when she messes with your family then own up to your words!! and don't go blindly trusting her & taking her side whenever you get a chance, be for real. he's basically naivety incarnate!! like what even was that 'trust me' speech 😭 anywho, James is a mix of Kenji & Aaron — like yk with the looks of Warner but the personality of Kenji? yeah, that's James. he was so unintentionally funny which made his pov hilarious at times, especially when Kenji or Warner made an appearance!! unlike Rosa, he had always something to say, and it was really fun to read about him until he turned into brainless bubble of naivety.

ᝰ.ᐟ Rosabelle and James

aren't they just the most ethereal looking people walking on this earth!! ugh, how surprising. anyways, I feel scammed. they were marketed as enemies to lovers, and there was nothing of this sort here, but I could've seen that coming especially since authors nowadays try to sell anything as this trope. their relationship from the beginning to the end of this book felt like a total fever dream — they met like twice but acted like they were already planning their future together and couldn't stop rambling about how the other one was gorgeous!!! the insta attraction wasn't really it. what's more, there even wasn't any relationship development on their part. like why do they even like each other besides their looks? they gave me absolutely NOTHING. there was no tension, angst or chemistry between them — I mean, even my cats have more chemistry with each other.
